title: Marked nodal reduction of one relative curve
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper dominant morphism of excellent integral Noetherian schemes. Assume that $Y$ is projective [def-kun-projective] over the spectrum of a Noetherian ring. Let $y$ be the generic point of $Y$. Suppose $X_y$ is smooth, irreducible, and of dimension $1$. Let $Z\subset X$ be a nowhere dense closed subscheme whose generic fibre $Z_y$ is etale over $\kappa(y)$. Then there is a commutative square $f\circ a=b\circ f'$ with proper dominant generically finite maps $a:X'\to X$, $b:Y'\to Y$, $b$ projective, with excellent integral sources, and a projective flat finitely presented morphism $f':X'\to Y'$. Every geometric fibre of $f'$ is connected of pure dimension $1$ and has at worst ordinary double points. There are a nowhere dense closed subset $T\subset Y'$ and an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset X'$ such that $f'$ is smooth over $Y'\setminus T$, $D\to Y'$ is finite etale, $D$ is contained in the relative smooth locus, and $a^{-1}(|Z|)\subset |D|\cup (f')^{-1}(T)$. The generic fibre of $f'$ is smooth and geometrically integral. An ordinary double point on a geometric fibre means a point with completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, for its algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$. An effective Cartier divisor means a closed subscheme locally cut out by one non-zero-divisor. Generically finite means finite over a dense open in the target; its degree need not be invertible.

Conventions for the notions used here: properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]; integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme]; excellence [def-exc-excellent-ring]; Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; projectivity [def-kun-projective]; flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism]; finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; etaleness [def-weil-etale-morphism]; scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; geometric integrality, connectedness and reducedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]; finite morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Expose IX, Theorem 1.2 (i), (iii)--(vi), and the paragraph defining a nodal curve, printed p. 131; specialization of de Jong 1997, Theorem 2.4. The etale closed divisor is proper over the base, hence finite; geometric integrality of the generic fibre follows from smoothness and geometric connectedness. Exposé IX uses projectivity in the projective-bundle sense. Because $Y$ is projective over an affine scheme, $b$ and $f'$ are projective in the closed-immersion convention of the DAG: apply Stacks 087S (morphisms-lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective) to $b$ over $Y$, then 01WE (morphisms-lemma-H-projective-composition), then 087S again to $f'$ over $Y'$. For $a$ only properness is asserted.
